findings.title: IAM access key created without PGP encryption
findings.description: IAM access keys should be created with pgp_key so the secret access key is encrypted at creation. Without it, the plaintext secret is stored in Terraform state. Set pgp_key to a PGP public key.

evidence.expected: pgp_key set to a PGP public key

findings.remediation:
Rotate IAM access keys every 90 days or less. Prefer short-lived credentials:
federate via IAM Identity Center / SSO, or use instance profiles and ECS task roles
instead of long-lived keys. Audit with IAM Access Analyzer unused-access findings.

findings.title: IAM access key secret not encrypted with pgp_key
findings.description: An active access key is created without pgp_key, so the secret access key is stored in plaintext in the Terraform state. Anyone with state access can read the long-lived credential. Set pgp_key to encrypt the secret.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: IAM user has no tags
findings.description: The IAM user carries no tags, making ownership, purpose, and lifecycle untraceable in audits and complicating attribute-based access control. Tag identities with at least owner and purpose.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.
